All the recent edits to `src/tui.tsx` were focused on improving the handling of user input while a turn is already running. I added a comment explaining the unified ticker, inserted logic to queue new submissions when `running` is true, and updated the dependency list for the `submit` callback to include `running`. I also made sure the `submitRef` is set after the callback definition. 

Now I need to verify that these changes actually work in practice. The best way is to build the CLI, install the binary, and then run an interactive session where I can type a prompt while the model is still generating output. The existing test harness in the previous Bash command does exactly that: it compiles the TypeScript project, copies the resulting binary to `~/.local/bin`, launches a detached tmux session, sends a prompt, and captures the last few lines of output to see whether the prompt remains visible during generation.

When I ran that command earlier, it failed immediately with:

```
error TS5058: The specified path does not exist: 'tsconfig.json'.
cp: cannot stat 'dist/glint': No such file or directory
```

That tells me the command was executed from the wrong working directory – the shell was not in the `glint-cli` project root, so `tsconfig.json` couldn't be found and the build never produced `dist/glint`. To fix this, I must first `cd` into the project directory (`/home/lane/GR/glint-cli`) before invoking the TypeScript compiler and the subsequent build steps.

The rest of the pipeline can stay exactly the same: run `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` to type‑check, then `bun build src/index.tsx --compile --outfile dist/glint` to produce the binary, copy it to `~/.local/bin/glint`, and finally spin up a tmux session that runs `glint --no-intro`. After a short pause I’ll send the prompt “write a haiku about terminals” and capture the pane output to confirm that the prompt line stays on screen while the model streams its response.

Therefore, the next action is to issue a Bash command that first changes into the correct directory and then runs the same sequence of commands as before. This should give me a clean build and a concrete test of the new queuing behavior.

I'll construct the Bash tool call with the full command string, including the `cd` prefix and a descriptive note that this is building from the project directory and testing input visibility mid‑run.

arguments.command: cd /home/lane/GR/glint-cli && bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit && bun build src/index.tsx --compile --outfile dist/glint 2>&1 | tail -1 && tmux kill-session -t glint 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.8; cp dist/glint ~/.local/bin/glint && echo OK && tmux new-session -d -s glint -x 110 -y 38 -c /tmp/glint-test 'glint --no-intro 2>/tmp/glint-tui-err.log' && sleep 1.5 && tmux send-keys -t glint 'write a haiku about terminals' && sleep 0.2 && tmux send-keys -t glint Enter && sleep 1.5 && tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -10
arguments.description: Build from project dir, test input visibility mid-run
